name: Punk Graphics
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference, not a style directly named in the source collection. Uses cutout lettering, torn paper, tape, photocopy grain and handwritten marks in irregular layouts, with a prominent headline, distinct material edges and a limited palette.
suitableUses: Explicit fit: posters, title cards and short protest-style edits. Also useful for gig or campaign announcements, lyric clips, archival stories and editorial collage intros when slogans or a consistent print treatment are central. Broader narrative and HTML uses are inferred suitability.
limitations: The suggested colors are not canonical and yield to task, brand, reference and existing semantic colors. Red on the suggested paper color fails the stated normal-text contrast target; use red decoratively. Keep gradients disabled and don't recolor approved assets. Avoid excessive distortion or motion that obscures copy.
palette: Optional three-token suggestion: paper background #EFE9D9, ink foreground #171717, protest-red accent #C63A3A. Use discrete tokens; red is decorative, not for normal text on paper (4.26 contrast, below 4.5). Ink on paper is 14.793. Recheck actual compositing and preserve exact supplied colors and roles.
motionAndInteraction: Animate pasting, peeling and tearing with small deliberate placement imperfections. Keep movement abrupt and irregular, without springy motion, smooth tracking or random per-frame jitter. For video, drive deterministic states from seekable composition time. For interactive HTML, word-by-word scroll or button assembly is a compatible suggestion; keep real text accessible, provide reduced-motion static output, and make reverse scroll coherent. These interaction details come from suggested combinations, not the base style.
audio: No fixed soundtrack. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied choices and assets. Suggest mood, energy, tempo, voice and scene changes where useful, then synchronize and mix with picture. Avoid assuming audio assets exist.
assetRequirements: Prepare torn-paper masks and printed assets with Pillow; use fixed textures and deliberate placement. Photos may use precomputed monochrome halftone cutouts, while headlines remain solid. Rough.js is optional for seeded sketch contours, hachure or doodles; it does not create handwriting, paper texture, authentic print materials or animation. Preserve source assets and load fonts locally.
combinations: Use alone when cutout chaos carries the message. Optional pairing with style-093 adds timed headline and slogan delivery; style-050 supplies consistent monochrome halftone photo treatment. Respect their specific palette and red-use rules. Motion candidates are optional: chapter handoffs or storytelling only when narrative supports them; glitch cuts only for intentionally abrasive transitions that preserve legibility.
productionApproach: Choose visual and motion methods by style, action, assets and fidelity; the renderer owns artwork and the motion engine owns movement. Python/Pillow can preprocess assets; optional Rough.js handles seeded contours. HyperFrames is the primary assembly, timing, sync, validation and export pipeline. Use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or verified unable to meet a requirement, and record why. Keep video deterministic and seekable; interactive scroll/pointer input belongs to HTML delivery.
